topic: What the GFI 5% to 63% figure means
claim_a: GFI SOTIR 2023 and 10-charts page: share who would eat plant-based meat rises from 5% who eat it regularly now to 63% who would eat it always (15%) or often (48%) if all concerns were resolved (ECO-23; ECO-24)
claim_b: GFI press release Feb 2024: if cost and other challenges are resolved, three-quarters of Southeast Asian consumers say they would regularly consume plant-based meat (CON-02)
position_taken: Use 63% always or often, as charted with n=5,971. The three-quarters wording seems to count a broader group and is not shown in any chart we could read
notes: Both are hypothetical, regional and stated; neither is a forecast; no Vietnam split is public

claim_a: About 80% of soy milk (brief context, ECO-41, press from QNS filings, 2024)
claim_b: 90.6% of branded soy milk in 2024, up 1 point (Bao Viet Securities via CON-27; Mirae Asset CON-26)
position_taken: Use 90.6% of branded (packaged) soy milk for 2024; treat 80% as an older or broader-base figure
notes: Bases differ (branded packaged versus all soy milk, including fresh street soy milk); neither method is published

topic: How many Vietnamese have tried plant-based products
claim_a: Rakuten Insight 2025: 92% have tried plant-based alternatives (CON-07)
claim_b: GFI 2023: 42% have ever tried plant-based meat (CON-02)
position_taken: Both hold: Rakuten counts any plant-based alternative (89% of triers had plant milk); GFI counts plant-based meat only. Use GFI for meat analogues
notes: Rakuten 47% trial of plant-based meat alternatives is close to GFI 42%, but may include traditional mock meat

claim_a: Rakuten 2025: 43% consume plant-based alternatives several times a week (CON-07)
claim_b: GFI 2023: 3% eat plant-based meat one or more times a week (CON-02)
position_taken: Both hold; different categories. For product design use GFI for meat analogues and Rakuten for plant milk

topic: Awareness of novel alternative protein among Hanoi youth
claim_a: Nguyen M.Q. et al. 2025 text: 84% aware but not used (CON-12); RD-32 reports the same 84%
claim_b: Same paper: 202 of 288 respondents (70%) were aware but had not used
position_taken: Use 70% if anything, rated Low; the identical 84% in two samples suggests reuse

claim_a: Euromonitor: plant-based dairy retail value fell strongly in 2023 (CON-30)
claim_b: Google Trends: search interest in sữa hạt peaked in 2023 (index 82 against 44 in 2022) (CON-37)
position_taken: Prefer Euromonitor for sales; search interest is not sales and is driven by home nut-milk machines
notes: Consistent with a DIY shift: people searching how to make nut milk at home may buy less packaged product

topic: Who the early adopters are by age
claim_a: GFI 2023: 18 to 24 year olds are the least aware; about two-thirds of Enthusiasts are over 35 (CON-02)
claim_b: Vietnamese academic studies focus on 18 to 25 students and report high willingness (CON-12; CON-13; RD-32)
position_taken: Prefer GFI: target 25 to 44 urban earners; student intentions are cheap talk with low incomes
notes: Faunalytics literature review also names older (55+) health-conscious consumers (CON-05)

claim_a: GFI 2023: plant-based meat Expanders tend to be higher income; Rejectors lower (ECO-23)
claim_b: Delley et al. 2024: Vietnamese proactive meat reducers skew to the two lowest income bands (CON-08)
position_taken: Both hold: premium plant-based meat skews rich; meat reduction for health or money skews poorer and will use cheap chay and tofu, not premium analogues
notes: Different constructs (product use versus intention to cut meat)

claim_a: Nguyen M.Q. et al. 2025: environmental and sustainability concern raises attitude to novel protein (CON-12)
claim_b: Ly and Ly 2025: environmental concern has a small negative effect on intention (CON-13); Rakuten: environment ranks 6th of 7 reasons in Vietnam (CON-07)
position_taken: Treat environment as a weak and unstable driver in Vietnam; lead with health, safety and value
notes: Both academic samples are small and student-based

claim_a: Nguyen T.L. et al. 2020 (spirituality) and Nguyen T.Q.N. et al. 2025 (religious values) find positive effects; Rakuten: 35% cite following a vegetarian diet (CON-11; CON-16; CON-07)
claim_b: Ly and Ly 2025: religious beliefs not significant among Hanoi students (CON-13)
position_taken: Religion drives chay and periodic vegetarian demand among the general population, less so among students choosing modern products
notes: Seasonal search peaks for chay in August support the religious calendar effect (CON-37)

topic: Share of Vietnamese who eat vegetarian
claim_a: Unnamed 2019 survey in CafeF: 55% eat chay (CON-20)
claim_b: Delley et al. 2024: 4% of urban meat eaters call themselves flexitarian (CON-08)
position_taken: Reject the 55% (no source; arithmetic does not reconcile). The 4% excludes non-meat eaters and is urban only
notes: Definitions differ: occasional chay days versus a self-declared diet

claim_a: Press and consultancy figures: VND 1,000 billion plant-based meat (ECO-17), USD 500 million (ECO-18), USD 112 million vegan food 2025 (IMARC via CON-38)
claim_b: Revealed evidence: no Mintel launches 2022 to Q2 2023 (ECO-23); one imported analogue brand in 186 audited SKUs (FORM-01)
position_taken: Do not use the market-size claims; no method is traceable
notes: Branded soy milk alone is about VND 5,300 billion (our derivation), which suggests these figures lump in soy milk or chay
